entries.supports: A journalist’s account of the Rybinsk flooding figures and of the Leushino prayer ‘standings’ since 1999.
entries.limitation: Popular magazine feature read in full in the built-in browser; figures have no references; one claim (a report of 294 residents who chose to remain, attributed to an NKVD document in the Rybinsk museum) is not used because it is unverified. Page numbers are read from one running head.

entries.author: Koroleva, S. Yu.; Chetina, E. M.; Kolegova, O. A.

entries.author: Zhigaltsova, T. V.
entries.title: Obrazno-emotsional'noe vospriiatie zhiteliami pozhilogo vozrasta zabroshennogo lesnogo poselka (Arkticheskaia territoriia Arkhangel'skoi oblasti)
entries.publisher: Izvestiia Komi nauchnogo tsentra UrO RAN (text on CyberLeninka)
entries.supports: Residents’ emotional map of a declining logging settlement; mentions of the cemetery and abandoned graves.
entries.limitation: Abstract and the passages mentioning the cemetery read in the built-in browser; re-checked on 2026-11-16 through a web-fetch summary of the page (machine summary): Izvestiia Komi nauchnogo tsentra UrO RAN, 2018, issue 1 (33), pp. 113–117, no DOI shown; 40 surveyed, 32 kept by age, 10 interviewees aged 50–80. 32 questionnaires and 10 interviews, one settlement; a psychology study, not about beliefs. The percentages belong to different emotion categories (pity: school 28.1%, abandoned houses 15.6%, hospital 12.5%; shame: dump 21%); an earlier version of the plate mixed them.

entries.author: Balabeikina, O. A.; Korobushchenko, V. Yu.; Mazurenko, A. A.
entries.title: Uprazdnennye poseleniia severo-vostochnykh raionov Respubliki Kareliia (1938–2005 gg.)
entries.publisher: Vestnik Pskovskogo gosudarstvennogo universiteta. Seriia: Estestvennye i fiziko-matematicheskie nauki, vol. 16, no. 1, pp. 3–12
entries.supports: Count of abolished settlements in four Karelian districts; legal basis; Pulozero and Petrovsky Yam items.
entries.limitation: Read in the built-in browser from the introduction to the section on tourism; the final paragraphs and the table’s fine print only skimmed. Based on legal decisions and online materials, not fieldwork; no counts of graves or visitors. Re-checked on 2026-11-16 through a web-fetch summary of the page (machine summary): 14 settlements, Art. 13 of 131-FZ criteria, Yuma 1989, Pulozero 1905 population 52, Petrovsky Yam 1982, hospital no. 2212 of the Karelian Front, 70 km route confirmed; ‘annual’ for the Memory Escort is not in the text (‘for several decades, on dates near the anniversary’); Soroka is a second exception (joined to Belomorsk).

entries.author: Samoilova, Elena
entries.title: Antropomorfnye figury v kontekste pokhoronno-pominal’noi obriadnosti severnorusskoi derevni

entries.publisher: Collection, Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (Kunstkamera), ISBN 978-5-88431-209-8, pp. 252–268
entries.supports: A figure made from the dead person’s clothing, kept in the red corner until the fortieth day; who started and who kept it; the author’s limits on her evidence.
entries.limitation: Read from the owner’s PDF (18 pages): pp. 251–255 and 265–268 closely, the rest searched for key words, not read through. Few cases: three for 1910–1940, four named informants; O. Konshin’s originals burned in 2007 and were partly restored from memory. A first version of this entry relied on two web-fetch summaries, one of which wrongly turned a fairy-tale passage (the mother’s gift of a doll to her daughter) into ritual feeding; that is corrected. The volume title and year are not on the pages.

entries.author: Sokolova, A. (initials ‘A. S.’ in the footnotes; name from the page title)

entries.title: Moscow burial services being privatized
entries.supports: That in June 2012 the head of Moscow’s trade and services department said commercial burial functions would pass from the municipal company Ritual to private firms; the market was estimated at over 12 billion rubles; cremation was 44% of Moscow burials; Moscow had 71 cemeteries, two open to new burials.
